title: [UNDER CONSTRUCTION] A Non-Local Formulation of Water Waves
text:
(1.1) A new non-local formulation of water waves in three dimensions
We start by defining the domain
\[
D=\{-\infty<x_j<\infty,\quad j=1,2,\quad -h<y<\eta(x_1, x_2, t),\quad t>0\}
\]
The classical gravity water wave problem satisfies
\[
\Delta\phi=0\quad\text{in }D,
\] \[
\phi_y=0\quad\text{on }y=-h,
\] \[
\eta_t+\phi_{x_1}\eta_{x_1}+\phi_{x_2}\eta_{x_2}=\phi_y\quad\text{on }y=\eta,
\tag{1}\] \[
\phi_t+\frac{1}{2}|\nabla\phi|^2+g\eta=\frac{\sigma}{\rho}\nabla\cdot\left(\frac{\nabla\eta}{\sqrt{1+|\nabla\eta|^2}}\right)\quad\text{on }y=\eta.
\]
We aim to reformulate these equations purely in terms of functions on the free boundary. These functions are \(\eta(x_1, x_2, t)\) and \(q(x_1, x_2, t):=\phi(x_1, x_2, \eta(x_1, x_2, t), t)\).
Since Equation 1 is satisfied on the free surface, and
\[
\phi_{x_1}+\phi_y\eta_{x_1}=q_{x_1},
\] \[
\phi_{x_2}+\phi_y\eta_{x_2}=q_{x_2},
\]
we can create the linear system
\[
\begin{bmatrix}
    \phi_{x_1} \\
    \phi_{x_2}
\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
    -\eta_{x_1}^2 & -\eta_{x_1}\eta_{x_2} \\
    -\eta_{x_1}\eta_{x_2} & -\eta_{x_2}^2
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}
    \phi_{x_1} \\
    \phi_{x_2}
\end{bmatrix}
+
\begin{bmatrix}
    q_{x_1}-\eta_{x_1}\eta_t \\
    q_{x_2}-\eta_{x_2}\eta_t
\end{bmatrix}
\] \[
\implies
\begin{bmatrix}
    1+\eta_{x_1}^2 & \eta_{x_1}\eta_{x_2} \\
    \eta_{x_1}\eta_{x_2} & 1+\eta_{x_2}^2
\end{bmatrix}
\begin{bmatrix}
    \phi_{x_1} \\
    \phi_{x_2}
\end{bmatrix}
=
\begin{bmatrix}
    q_{x_1}-\eta_{x_1}\eta_t \\
    q_{x_2}-\eta_{x_2}\eta_t
\end{bmatrix}.
\]
The solution of which is
\[
\phi_{x_1}=\frac{(1+\eta_{x_2}^2)q_{x_1}-\eta_{x_1}\eta_{x_2}q_{x_2}-\eta_{x_1}\eta_t}{1+|\nabla\eta|^2},
\] \[
\phi_{x_2}=\frac{(1+\eta_{x_1}^2)q_{x_2}-\eta_{x_1}\eta_{x_2}q_{x_1}-\eta_{x_2}\eta_t}{1+|\nabla\eta|^2},
\] \[
\phi_y=\frac{\eta_t+\eta_{x_1}q_{x_1}+\eta_{x_2}q_{x_2}}{1+|\nabla\eta|^2}.
\]
At this point, the authors suggest that
\[
|\nabla\phi|^2=\frac{(1+\eta_{x_2}^2)q_{x_1}^2+(1+\eta_{x_1}^2)q_{x_2}^2+\eta_t^2-2\eta_{x_1}\eta_{x_2}q_{x_1}q_{x_2}}{1+|\nabla\eta|^2}.
\tag{2}\]
Rather than deriving Equation 2 from scratch, we can more easily verify its validity by showing that \[
[1+|\nabla\eta|^2]\cdot[(1+\eta_{x_2}^2)q_{x_1}^2+(1+\eta_{x_1}^2)q_{x_2}^2+\eta_t^2-2\eta_{x_1}\eta_{x_2}q_{x_1}q_{x_2}]
\] \[
=[(1+\eta_{x_2}^2)q_{x_1}-\eta_{x_1}\eta_{x_2}q_{x_2}-\eta_{x_1}\eta_t]^2+[(1+\eta_{x_1}^2)q_{x_2}-\eta_{x_1}\eta_{x_2}q_{x_1}-\eta_{x_2}\eta_t]^2+[\eta_t+\eta_{x_1}q_{x_1}+\eta_{x_2}q_{x_2}]^2,
\]
since \((1+|\nabla\eta|^2)\) must be a factor in the numerator of \(\phi_{x_1}^2+\phi_{x_2}^2+\phi_y^2\) for Equation 2 to hold.
